""" Send an email to Bob with FL658038 flight details. Usage: 1. Update the configuration section below with your SMTP and recipient details. 2. Run: python send_flight_email.py """ import smtplib from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart from email.mime.text import MIMEText from email.mime.base import MIMEBase from email import encoders import os # ────────────────────────────────────────────── # Configuration – update these before running # ────────────────────────────────────────────── SMTP_SERVER = "smtp.example.com" # e.g. "smtp.gmail.com" SMTP_PORT = 587 SENDER_EMAIL = "alice@example.com" SENDER_PASSWORD = "your_password" # or use an app-specific password RECIPIENT_EMAIL = "bob@example.com" ICS_FILE_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "flight_FL658038.ics") # ────────────────────────────────────────────── # Flight details # ────────────────────────────────────────────── FLIGHT = { "number": "FL658038", "origin": "JFK (New York)", "destination": "LHR (London)", "departure": "2026-10-15 at 19:00 UTC", "arrival": "2026-10-16 at 07:00 UTC", } # ────────────────────────────────────────────── # Build email # ────────────────────────────────────────────── def build_email(): msg = MIMEMultipart("mixed") msg["From"] = SENDER_EMAIL msg["To"] = RECIPIENT_EMAIL msg["Subject"] = f"Flight Update: {FLIGHT['number']} — {FLIGHT['origin']} ✈ {FLIGHT['destination']}" # Plain-text body text_body = ( f"Hi Bob,\n\n" f"Here are the details for the upcoming flight:\n\n" f" Flight Number : {FLIGHT['number']}\n" f" From : {FLIGHT['origin']}\n" f" To : {FLIGHT['destination']}\n" f" Departure : {FLIGHT['departure']}\n" f" Arrival : {FLIGHT['arrival']}\n\n" f"I've attached a calendar (.ics) file so you can add it to your calendar.\n\n" f"Best regards,\n" f"Alice" ) # HTML body html_body = f"""\

Hi Bob,

Here are the details for the upcoming flight:

Flight Number{FLIGHT['number']}
From{FLIGHT['origin']}
To{FLIGHT['destination']}
Departure{FLIGHT['departure']}
Arrival{FLIGHT['arrival']}

I've attached a calendar (.ics) file so you can add it to your calendar.

Best regards,
Alice

""" # Attach text + HTML alternatives alt_part = MIMEMultipart("alternative") alt_part.attach(MIMEText(text_body, "plain")) alt_part.attach(MIMEText(html_body, "html")) msg.attach(alt_part) # Attach .ics file if os.path.exists(ICS_FILE_PATH): with open(ICS_FILE_PATH, "rb") as f: ics_attachment = MIMEBase("text", "calendar", method="PUBLISH", name="flight_FL658038.ics") ics_attachment.set_payload(f.read()) encoders.encode_base64(ics_attachment) ics_attachment.add_header("Content-Disposition", "attachment", filename="flight_FL658038.ics") msg.attach(ics_attachment) print(f"✔ Attached: {ICS_FILE_PATH}") else: print(f"⚠ ICS file not found at {ICS_FILE_PATH} — sending without attachment.") return msg def send_email(): msg = build_email() try: with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_SERVER, SMTP_PORT) as server: server.ehlo() server.starttls() server.ehlo() server.login(SENDER_EMAIL, SENDER_PASSWORD) server.sendmail(SENDER_EMAIL, RECIPIENT_EMAIL, msg.as_string()) print(f"✔ Email sent successfully to {RECIPIENT_EMAIL}") except smtplib.SMTPAuthenticationError: print("✖ Authentication failed. Check your email/password (or use an app password).") except smtplib.SMTPException as e: print(f"✖ SMTP error: {e}") except ConnectionRefusedError: print(f"✖ Could not connect to {SMTP_SERVER}:{SMTP_PORT}. Check your SMTP settings.") if __name__ == "__main__": send_email()
